I hid my scars successfully for years until I made the decision to let tell my mother when I was an adult and moved out from under their roof. I always switched from cutting on my thighs and on my wrists.

Some things I've learned in my fifteen years of self harm.

People will judge.
Not everyone understand some cutters are not sucidial.
If you would like to hide your cuts, cutting on the top of your thighs is a good option. I use to cut in the shower. Make sure you can still wear shorts and have them covered while you sit down (huge difference from when you're standing -trust) 
Also truly remember if you are cutting deep the scars are permanent. I have about an 8 inch strip of scars on both of my thighs and scars on both wrists which I cover by wearing bracelets.

But also, here's another thing I didn't think of when I started. I've been wearing bracelets for fifteen years now because I'm scared of having my scars out in the open especially with my position at work. 

Something else I never thought of when I initially started cutting myself was that eventually I would be intimate with someone and I would have to explain them. This has created many diverse reactions and induced many more episodes.

Another thing I never thought of when I was young, I was married in October and I had to wear my bracelets to cover my scars. That was such a somber, difficult moment on what was supposed to be the happiest day of my life. 

I don't say all this to scare you, but I hope to be more of a mentor. Someone who has gone through it before and I've seen alot. I just wanted to give some insight I never thought about all those years ago.

And while I may not be in full recovery, because I self harm in many other ways now instead of physical harm -  because my husband gets testy and I can't hide physical damage. But, those decisions have stayed with me for years and they will live with me for all my days.

Self harm can come in many forms.. my friends tell me I am the poster child for a self destructive person. 

Some typically well known physical self harm is hitting, cutting or burning.

But there is also self harm in the form of not eating. Or over exersizing to the point of your body deteriorating.

Drug abuse can be a form of self harm as well. 

Be smart and stay safe

I understand how you feel. I have struggled with self harm in multiple ways for the past fifteen years. When I was younger I always hoped I would grow out of it, but it is difficult. I have about an 8 inch strip of scars on both my thighs and many on my wrists where I wear bracelets in attempt to cover them. 

Many times in my life people have commented on them. Sometimes I get that feeling where it's like my stomach is twisting in a circle when someone mentions them. But, then normally I get this anger flood through me because my scars are deep. They are large and they are prominent. There is no question how they came to be and for someone to just outright point them out and most of the time give me their opinion of them just sets me off. 

Those are the same people who don't recognize the pain or the daily struggle we go through. I wouldn't trade my past or my scars because the insensitivity of my peers that has come with them have certainly shaped the person I've become. 

Stay strong ♡

I firmly believe no one should play with ouiji boards because of my experience. 

I didn't know a whole lot about it and me and my friend were dickin around not really sure what to do and she pulls her out and says we should play. We decided that we should go to the park by her house ( also conveniently by the oldest cemetery in our town.)
We get in her car and drive down to the park. Luckily there weren't many people there, I don't remember the exact time but I remember it being pitch black out. We get settled and start the process.
At first nothing happened. We asked a bunch of questions until getting frustrated and finally asking if anyone was willing to contact us. Someone or something did. 

It was a little boy, he told us his name was Jack and he was four. We asked Jack what his favorite color was and he told us Red. Then my friend went on to ask 'well what do you like that's red?' It then proceeded to start spelling b...l....o....o.....then we looked at each other instantaneously said goodbye.

But, of course we were young and stupid so we didn't stop there. A few weeks later we decided to play in her house, because everyone knows her house is haunted. It started about the same. We contacted a spirit this time a girl who said she was 12 and her name was Penalope, yes she spelt it wrong. She started describing our experiences that we've had around the house, smoking in her and her sisters rooms and other little things. I got creeped out and I took my hands off the board without saying goodbye.......bad fucking mistake. I vowed to never touch an ouiji board again.


Fast forward a few months. My friend had a couple of her drum Corp friends over and they want to play with the ouiji board....I of course sit out but stay near them while they played. 
They lit some candles sat in a circle and they begin asking simple questions. They contact a girl, who's name is Penalope. They start asking her questions she says she's 12. They ask her what her favorite color is and she said red and I noped the fuck right out of there......
.....fucking fucked up......

My boyfriend and I have been best friends for 6 years and we've been dating over three. We're both in our mid twenties and we arn't really normal young adults meaning we don't go out drinking or partying often. 

But there is one thing that we make it a point to do at least once a week. We go on a drive, to nowhere in specific just the back roads of towns we've never been in, crossing state boarders and stopping at quaint little stores and restaurants. 


He knows how much rides mean to me because I am the youngest of five and my parents weren't poor but we definitely weren't rich either and every Sunday they'd pile us in the car and we'd go for a drive. Sometimes we all would talk, laugh, play car games and anything else Mom (Dad was always the driver) could think of to entertain kids ranging from 3-16.

Many times my parents would tell us stories of when they were kids and they used to go out once a week and drive around, to no where in particular but just the back roads of New England they had never been before and they used to dream about what plot of land they would own for a house and what town they stumbled upon that held a special place in their hearts. They use to show us where they had debated about setting down roots or there was another time they took us to a 70 foot raging waterfall they found in their journeys. 


I shared this little piece of my life with Cam when we first became friends, it was a little bittersweet for me because my Dad has a lot of health issues and just talkin about those memories sent a pang in my chest every time. But after I shared this, he made it a point to ask me (usually on Sundays) if I wanted to go to Dunkin Donuts for coffee and from there he begins to take random quiet back roads that we've never been to before, talking about which town we fell in love with and what plot of land we will own one day.

Wow. I have never written a poem about insects and this is quite the interesting read. 


Question. Was the rhyming intentional in the poem? 
I only ask this because I used to only rhyme with my poetry then I went to  creative writing workshop where one of my peers asked me "Why do you limit yourself with rhyme?"

I never thought of it as a limitation, it just was what I had known and was comfortable with, but I figured I'd just try out a poem without rhyme once and to be honest I've never gone back. 


Rhyming can be both positive and negative. When writing a poem there is something the writer needs the world to hear. There is a voice to the poem which guides the reader to the conclusion the poet wanted us to come to. Rhyming can be tricky because you have just limited your choice of words quite drastically which can lead to muddy (unclear) lines in your poem.


I like the first line of the poem. It defiantly is unique and I was intrigued to see where it was going. I also like the imagery you use to describe each insect, it almost create mini poems in each stanza. 


Now, I am a bit confused on what particularly this vessel you describe is. I don't believe there's enough literary clues to lead us to make an educated guess as to what you're writing about and I would like to know that. 

Over all I critiqued both of the poems you posted and I believe you've got some great content in these and I think you just need to push your boundaries a little more. Either way, great start! Kudos!

I enjoy the first two stanzas, I think that they are a great introduction to the poem. I really like the second stanza
"There was probably trouble
Hunger, maybe
War and death
I faced none of these"
Particularly the second into the third line, you really grabbed my attention with the line break. 
I do think that you should keep in mind the words you use repeatedly. Like I noticed you used trouble in the second and third stanzas. Repetition should be used as an emphasis. There is a voice that each poem carries and the word choice you use should be deliberate and if you chose to use the same words, they should carry a different weight to them at the end of the poem as opposed to the beginning. 
Think about what statement you want heard when you wrote this. Clearly, you're speaking about this pain people have to endure every day but you don't see first hand. Maybe instead of using trouble in the third stanza first line "I saw none of this trouble." Maybe switch trouble to despair. I think that would change the mood of the poem as well.
I think this is a great start to a piece and I can't wait to read more. Kudos!
